findings.sentence: **The backends the fleet never runs.** The audit closes on the three crates no host exercises: backend-kde hard-fails without a session bus (`Connection::session().await?` at `backend-kde/src/lib.rs:41`) and has zero fleet consumers because no jupiterOS host runs Plasma — greps for plasma/kde across hosts and modules return nothing, and the hard-fail is the stated boundary condition for ever hosting a desktop class (it must adopt the generic backend's warn-and-continue degradation first); backend-gamescope's only fleet consumer is callisto's arcade session, with kiosks reaching gamescope via the shared dashboard-gaming modeSpecs; backend-lutris ships behind the `jupiter.gaming.console` appCatalog but no host configuration exercises its launch-only buttons, its JSON field names hedged unverified — gamescope and lutris both among the backends the repo itself flags "Unverified in a live environment" [[interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class]] [[repo-map-ha-linux-agent]] [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]].
findings.reason: repo-map carries only the structural inventory of the three crates (file paths, symbols, symbol line numbers); it states none of the sentence's claims — no hard-fail detail, no fleet-consumer facts, no Plasma greps, no appCatalog, no unverified flags. The load-bearing legs are carried by the two co-cited interim notes.
findings.suggested_fix: optional: drop [[repo-map-ha-linux-agent]] from this sentence, or keep it solely as structural corroboration of the crates' existence — no text change required

findings.sentence: A dead `tls` knob sits at `config.rs:88`, the README has drifted (backend-hardware undocumented; zfs, syncthing, and lutris flagged by the repo itself as "Unverified in a live environment"), and the hardware backend exposes placeholder select options rather than sysfs-enumerated values [[interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict]].
findings.reason: the note carries only the zfs/syncthing/lutris-unverified leg ("three backends explicitly flagged 'Unverified in a live environment' (zfs, syncthing REST fields, lutris JSON field names — README's own words)"). The dead-tls-knob fact lives in interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class ("config.rs:88 parses mqtt.tls, agent.rs never calls set_transport — grep returns 0 hits") and appears nowhere in the cited note; the README-drift / backend-hardware-undocumented leg appears in no vault note (it is true against the repo directly — README.md has no backend-hardware section — but is uncited); the "placeholder select options rather than sysfs-enumerated values" leg appears in no note and is contradicted by the source: crates/backend-hardware/src/lib.rs:74-93 reads scaling_available_governors and energy_performance_available_preferences from sysfs, with hardcoded lists only as fallback on read failure.
findings.suggested_fix: re-cite the tls clause to [[interim-report-fleet-service-model-by-host-class]]; delete the placeholder-select clause (false per source — the options ARE sysfs-enumerated with fallback defaults); keep the adopt-vs-build citation only for the unverified-flags clause; ground the README-drift clause in a citable note or drop it

findings.sentence: rumqttc defaults to `clean_session=true`, keepalive 60 s, inflight 100 [[librs]], and callisto's mosquitto sets no `persistence`, so the default applies — "stored in memory only" — meaning every broker restart wipes all sessions fleet-wide [[mosquittoconf-man-page-eclipse-mosquitto]].
findings.reason: the note carries the persistence default ("If false, the data will be stored in memory only. Defaults to false") verbatim; the "callisto's mosquitto sets no persistence" connector is fleet ground truth documented in interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec (mqtt.nix sets only port/anonymous/users — no persistence), which this sentence does not cite.
findings.suggested_fix: add [[interim-report-mqtt-lifecycle-supervisor-spec]] to the sentence for the callisto mqtt.nix audit leg

findings.sentence: One calibration keeps the sizing honest: at the fleet's measured ~25 entities per host the default 1000 never binds — the binding quantity in #135266 was HA's own `#`-wildcard client against broker-wide retained replay — so the broker work is cheap hygiene plus a `$SYS` confirmation check on `$SYS/broker/publish/messages/dropped` (not the never-published `$SYS/broker/mqtt/*` variants mosquitto 2.1.2 excludes) rather than urgent resizing [[documentation-on-sysbrokermqtt-topics-is-wrong-issue-3726-eclipse-mosquittomosqu]] [[no-data-in-sysbrokermessagesinflight-issue-3021-eclipse-mosquittomosquitto-githu]].
findings.reason: the note carries the $SYS legs verbatim (/broker/publish/messages/dropped named as load-bearing; $SYS/broker/mqtt/* "never published, as of version 2.1.2"), but the "fleet's measured ~25 entities per host the default 1000 never binds" measurement and the "HA's own #-wildcard client" attribution are in neither cited note — the ~25-entity measurement exists only in the run's step-8 binding update (comparisons.md, not a vault note; the depth critic explicitly flagged it as having "no vault-note citation target"), and the #-wildcard/binding-quantity fact is carried by the databasec and comments notes, which this sentence does not cite.
findings.suggested_fix: keep the 3726 citation on the $SYS-topic clause only; anchor the ~25-entity sizing to a citable record or soften to "at the fleet's current per-host entity counts (tens, not thousands)"; optionally re-cite the #-wildcard leg to [[databasec]] or [[comments]]

findings.sentence: **The sensor bar.** go-hass-agent (v14.15.1, 2026-08-09, packaged in nixpkgs — the NixOS package collection — for all 24 Linux platforms, ~monthly cosign-signed releases) sources its Linux surface from D-Bus (logind sessions, power state, screen lock, NetworkManager, XDG portal, UPower, MPRIS, fwupd), ProcFS (memory, disk, load, per-core CPU usage and frequency, uptime, kernel, CPU vulnerabilities), SysFS (disk I/O rates, hwmon), and Netlink (link states, rates) [[github-joshuargo-hass-agent-a-home-assistant-native-app-for-desktoplaptop-device]] [[go-hass-agent-mynixos]].
findings.reason: mynixos carries v14.15.1-in-nixpkgs, the 24-platform build list, and the not-broken/insecure/unfree status, but not the "2026-08-09" release date or the "~monthly cosign-signed releases" cadence — both live in releases-joshuargo-hass-agent-github, which this sentence does not cite (its citations are the README note and mynixos).
findings.suggested_fix: add [[releases-joshuargo-hass-agent-github]] to the citation set for the date and cadence legs (or drop the date)

findings.sentence: Its users hit the wall in January 2026: a PipeWire output-device selector "can't be expressed" because the commands vocabulary has no dropdown [[go-hass-agent-a-native-app-integration-for-desktoplaptop-devices-share-your-proj]]. jupiterOS's session-switching requires a select whose options reflect real systemd unit state — grouped launcher profiles become one mutually exclusive select, the shared state topic reshaping through discovery — a vocabulary the incumbent architecturally lacks. lnxlink ships dropdowns (a Steam game-launcher select among them) and systemd unit control, but no mutual-exclusion semantics and no state round-trip tied to fleet power services [[lnxlink]].
findings.reason: the note carries January 2026, the PipeWire/pulseaudio output-selector request, and the no-dropdown facts, but the quoted phrase "can't be expressed" does not appear in the thread (0 hits for any form of "express" in the user's words); the source's verbatim words are "I can't see a means to do a drop-down selector box with multiple text items" — quotation marks are placed around a paraphrase.
findings.suggested_fix: replace the quoted "can't be expressed" with the source's verbatim words, or remove the quotation marks so it reads as paraphrase rather than quotation

findings.sentence: Its maintainer designs the systemd path for servers ("The systemctl service is primarily for 'headless' usage (i.e., servers)"), its changelog shows it paying the MQTT lifecycle dues in public — "reconnect to MQTT on disconnect and fix issue with MQTT commands not working", graceful channel shutdown, constant device ids — and it carries SMART with capability handling, per-core frequencies, link rates, OOM events, fwupd firmware security [[changelogmd]] [[github-joshuargo-hass-agent-a-home-assistant-native-app-for-desktoplaptop-device]]. lnxlink covers the desktop long tail, including a Steam game-launcher dropdown, a Lutris launcher dropdown shipped as a custom module, and a bash-command module creating sensors, buttons, and switches from shell scripts [[lnxlink]].
findings.reason: the README note carries the sensor legs (SMART with capability handling via cap_sys_rawio/sys_admin/mknod/dac_override, per-core CPU frequency, link states/rates via Netlink, OOM events via systemd-oomd, fwupd firmware security) and changelogmd carries the changelog legs, but the quoted "The systemctl service is primarily for 'headless' usage (i.e., servers)" appears in neither cited note — it lives verbatim in running-the-agent-as-a-service-and-tray-icon-joshuargo-hass-agent-discussion-387 (the maintainer's discussion #387 reply, quoted by the adopt-vs-build interim).
findings.suggested_fix: add [[running-the-agent-as-a-service-and-tray-icon-joshuargo-hass-agent-discussion-387]] to the maintainer-quote clause (or cite interim-report-adopt-vs-build-honest-verdict, which quotes it)
